summary: Federated principal mapping fails: identity-hash collapse causes routing to wrong account
description:
Issue summary:
Multiple service principals recently started receiving 403/401 errors when the federated attribute mapping runs during cross-cloud assumeRole/WIF flows. The identity-mapper component appears to normalize the incoming principal attribute (principalArn/principalSubject) into a 32-bit hash token; collisions cause attributes from different ARNs to collapse to the same token which then routes requests to the wrong account bucket in the orchestrator layer.

Impact:
- A small percentage (~0.5%) of cross-cloud requests that rely on STS/WIF federation fail authorization or get routed to an unrelated tenant's debug path.
- Visible failures in production: short-lived 5xx spikes on the federation proxy, some dedicated provisioning jobs fail with permission denied.

Environment:
- Production federation proxy in us-east (service: aws-gcp-federation-proxy v2.3.1)
- Identity-mapper: 1.8.0 running as a k8s deployment in redwood-federation-prod namespace
- Orchestrator routing rules: tag=env:prod, routing-table v12

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Simulate a STS assumeRole with long ARN including a service-account email-style subject (>180 characters).
2) Send repeated parallel requests (burst of 200) through the federation-proxy to exchange credentials.
3) Watch logs from identity-mapper: normalization step outputs a 32-bit hash token.
4) Compare routing decisions in orchestrator: two different ARNs map to same token and routing sends one to the other's bucket.

Observed behavior:
- identity-mapper log: "normalized_token=0x8f3a1b2c -> collapsed true" for two different subjects within same minute
- federation-proxy: intermittent 403s and a small number of 502s downstream for affected requests

Expected behavior:
- Unique principals map to unique routing tokens (no collisions within active namespace)
- When a hash collision happens, fallback should use full attribute compare rather than routing by token alone.

Relevant log snippets (sanitized):
- identity-mapper: "2026-03-10T18:02:15Z INFO incoming_subject=projects/123/serviceAccounts/very-long-service-account-email@example.com normalized_token=0x8f3a1b2c collapsed=false"
- identity-mapper: "2026-03-10T18:02:17Z INFO incoming_subject=arn:aws:iam::987654321:role/long-role-name normalized_token=0x8f3a1b2c collapsed=true candidates=[0x8f3a1b2c,0x4b2f9a11]"
- orchestrator: "2026-03-10T18:02:17Z WARN token-mismatch routing-request token=0x8f3a1b2c expected-owner=acct-98765 actual-owner=acct-11223"

Timing and frequency:
- First observed 2026-03-08, low cadence during weekend, spike during peak deploy traffic 2026-03-10 17:30-19:00 UTC
- Affects ~0.4-0.7% of federation requests in the window

Immediate mitigation tried:
- Rolled identity-mapper to a previous build (1.7.2) in prod-canary cluster: collision rate reduced to zero in canary but cannot fully roll back globally due to dependent schema change in orchestrator.
- Added additional logging and a temporary circuit in orchestrator to re-validate full principal string if candidate-token has seen a mismatch within last 5 minutes. That reduced customer-visible 403s by ~60% but increased request latency by ~30ms.

Notes:
- This problem is deterministic when input principal strings exceed ~128 bytes and include non-standard separators (colons, slashes, periods).
- The normalization function was changed in 1.8.0 to shorten tokens to 32 bits for performance; previously it used 128-bit truncated tokens.
comments: 2026-03-10T19:03Z - Jordan Li: Confirmed we have token duplicates in identity-mapper logs. I'll reproduce locally with recorded ARNs and a test harness.
2026-03-10T19:25Z - SRE Team (channel #infra-federation): Added temporary orchestrator fallback that compares full principal strings on mismatch; pushing as a stop-gap to reduce 403s.

2026-03-11T09:12Z - Priya Nair (Security): Need to confirm rollback surface re: schema change. If we revert identity-mapper to 1.7.2 we must ensure orchestrator still understands token format. Priya assigned to validate compatibility.

2026-03-12T02:48Z - Marcus Chen (Runtime): I've reproduced collision locally using two crafted principal subjects. Patch candidate: switch back to 128-bit token and add a post-hash equality check before routing. Preparing PR.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: 32-bit token space too small given cardinality of long-service-account strings and leads to collisions under burst traffic.
Hypothesis 2: Normalizer uses non-stable canonicalization for separators; same logical identity can map differently depending on input encoding (we've seen URL-encoded vs plain).
Partial finding: Running test harness with 10k synthetic ARNs produced ~0.65% collision rate at 32-bit hash; 128-bit truncated hash showed no collisions in same sample.
Telemetry: Added metric identity_mapper.hash_collisions and instrumented orchestrator to emit when fallback full-compare triggers. Collision metric today: 62 collisions over 24h (prod).
Compatibility check: Orchestrator routing-table currently assumes 32-bit token key. Changing token length requires coordinated rollout or feature flag.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: orchestrator will perform full principal string compare when token mismatch detected in last 10 minutes. This is deployed as emergency fix and documented in runbook.

Planned fix: revert to 128-bit truncated token in identity-mapper and add post-hash verification (full compare) as a defensive check. This requires orchestrator support via feature flag for token size compatibility.

Next steps: 1) PR #789 to identity-mapper (reintroduce 128-bit fallback + unit tests) 2) Orchestrator feature flag to accept expanded token size and gradual rollout 3) Post-deploy telemetry review and canary for 48h.
Owner: Marcus Chen (Runtime) for mapper change; Jordan Li (SRE) for orchestrator rollout. Target ETA for full fix: 2026-03-18.
Follow-up: Add chaos test to federation CI to intentionally create long-principal collisions and assert fallback behavior.
